original_title: Somalia: Belgium’s contribution through the Special Fund for Emergency and Resilience Activities (SFERA)
title: Somalia: Belgium’s contribution through the Special Fund for Emergency and Resilience Activities (SFERA)
original_summary:
Country: Somalia
Source: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

Please refer to the attached file.

The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) and Belgium support anticipatory action and flood early warning

Somalia remains one of the most climate-vulnerable countries globally, facing recurrent and compounding drought and flood cycles that erode livelihoods, displace populations and undermine food security. Between April and June 2026, an estimated 6 million people are projected to face Crisis or worse levels of acute food insecurity (IPC Phase 3 or above), including 1.9 million in Emergency (IPC Phase 4).1

Prolonged conflict, economic pressures, reduced humanitarian funding and access constraints have significantly reduced the delivery of critical assistance. Rising global fuel costs linked to the Strait of Hormuz crisis are increasing transport costs and disrupting supply chains in a country heavily dependent on food imports.

Extended drought conditions have led to severe water shortages and concomitant crop failures, livestock losses and widespread displacement. There is an over 90-percent probability of El Niño conditions developing from mid-2026 and intensifying during the October–December deyr season. This is expected to result in heavy rainfall, elevated river levels and a high risk of flooding, particularly along the Juba and Shabelle basins.

Previous floods throughout the last 30 years have caused extensive loss of life, displacement and damage to infrastructure. Current projections indicate that the 2026 El Niño could reach similar or higher levels of severity. According to FAO’s Somalia Water and Land Information Management analysis, 274 536 people who live along the Shabelle river floodplain are at risk.

Through SFERA, the Government of Belgium has contributed USD 1 013 818 to FAO for the implementation of anticipatory actions in Somalia, in collaboration with government and local partners. In Jowhar, early warning messages will be disseminated to the 274 536 people at risk of flooding, to enable timely evacuations, while flood mitigation activities, including debris clearing around the Sabuun barrage, will benefit approximately 269 000 people. In addition, nearly 38 000 of the most vulnerable people will receive forecast-based anticipatory cash assistance to support their immediate needs and safe relocation.

Anticipatory actions will be carried out ahead of the projected deyr flooding season (October–December 2026) with a focus on the Jowhar Off-Stream Storage Programme command area. Through improved risk forecasting, early warning systems and household preparedness, vulnerable communities will be better equipped to withstand floods.

original_title: US, Israel agree to pause further strikes on Iran after weeks of violence
title: US, Israel agree to pause further strikes on Iran after weeks of violence
original_summary: After weeks of escalating attacks and fears of an even wider war, President Donald Trump says the US and Israel have agreed to pause further strikes on Iran if a deal to end the conflict can be reached quickly. The announcement marks a dramatic change in tone after Trump recently warned Iran it would be hit "very hard". Iran swiftly denied there was any such agreement, dismissing Trump's account and casting fresh doubt over whether diplomacy is any closer.
